- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >10%), model overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome is significantly below historical mean (e.g., 3σ below), model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast upward by 3–8% to reflect reversion.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates in early periods when sentiment is volatile; add 1–3% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment is mixed or rising.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.33” values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 2–5% to capture latent upward bias.
